content.overview: BNS s. 26 — Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit. BNS restatement of IPC 88. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 88. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 26 is the rule on “Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit”. The section provides that nothing, which is not intended to cause death, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause, or be known by the doer to be likely to cause, to any person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, and who has given a consent, whether express or implied, to suffer that harm, or to take the risk of that harm. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 26 exists so that “Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit” has a closed legal test in Chapter III — General Exceptions. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: When an act is not an offence: mistake, accident, infancy, unsoundness, consent, compulsion — and the right of private defence.

The provision in detail
26. Nothing, which is not intended to cause death, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause, or be known by the doer to be likely to cause, to any person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, and who has given a consent, whether express or implied, to suffer that harm, or to take the risk of that harm

Essential ingredients
1. Nothing, which is not intended to cause death, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause, or be known by the doer to be likely to cause, to any person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, and who has given a consent, whether express or implied, to suffer that harm, or to take the risk of that harm

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, a surgeon, knowing that a particular operation is likely to cause the death of Z, who suffers under the painful complaint, but not intending to cause Z’s death, and intending, in good faith, Z’s benefit, performs that operation on Z, with Z’s consent. A has committed no offence

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 26 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.
